applies_from: P-1 onward, for the remainder of this invocation
statement: Every gate assertion and every verification script must emit a unique affirmative execution proof string at the end of its success path, of the form 'P1-CHECK-<id> PASSED', into a committed log. A judging tool reading that log treats a MISSING proof string as a FAIL for that check, identically to an assertion failure. Exit code 0 is not accepted as evidence that a check executed.
rationale: IMG-001 demonstrated that 'the verification step silently did not run at all' is a real failure mode, and it is far more dangerous than an assertion failure. A failed assertion is loud and stops the build. A verification layer that never executed is silent, exits 0, and manufactures confidence in an artifact nobody checked.
why_exit_code_is_insufficient: In IMG-001 the build step exited 0 precisely because nothing ran: the heredoc body was never delivered, python read empty stdin and terminated successfully. A success exit code was returned by a process that performed no verification, so exit status cannot distinguish 'passed' from 'never happened'.

requirements.the_judging_tool_enumerates_expected_che: so that a check which is silently removed is detected as missing rather than simply not looked for

strengthens: authority 9.4 traceability: a number whose verification cannot be shown to have run has no committed provenance
